correctness.rationale: For each y in the unit ball and each norming pair (x,x*), every point z of the hyperplane x*(z)=1 is at distance at least 1-x*(y) from y, while z_y=y+(1-x*(y))x lies on that hyperplane at exactly that distance. Taking the infimum proves eta=upsilon without compactness or attainment assumptions. Under symmetric Birkhoff orthogonality, w=y-x*(y)x is Birkhoff-orthogonal to x and hence ||w||<=||y||, yielding ||x-y||<=2-x*(y) and eta>=max(0,epsilon-1). For the affine-regular hexagon, the quarter-turn maps the dual hexagon onto the primal one, which directly gives Birkhoff symmetry; the two explicit y_epsilon families attain the lower bound on [0,1] and [1,2].
risks: The general Radon lower bound requires symmetric Birkhoff orthogonality; it is not asserted for arbitrary Banach spaces.
The finite checker supports the hexagonal geometry only; the universal eta=upsilon identity is established analytically.

value.rationale: The defining paper presents upsilon_X as a separate intermediate index between local convexity and eta_X. The universal identity shows that this auxiliary layer is redundant and converts the geometric distance definition of strong rotundity into an exact scalar support-deficit formula. That simplification applies to every real Banach space and directly sharpens how later results using both quantities can be read. The Radon lower bound then links the index to Birkhoff-symmetry geometry, and the affine-regular hexagon supplies a canonical exact non-Hilbert profile with a flat-to-linear phase change.
risks: The universal identity is elementary once the correct affine-hyperplane point is written down; its value is structural simplification and its consequences rather than technical depth.
